rules.title: Forbidding the Algorithmic Inflation of Rent (FAIR) Act
rules.requirement: Starting July 1, 2027, it is unlawful under the NJ Antitrust Act for landlords to pay for or use a coordinator's algorithmic software or device that performs a coordinating function, such as using other owners' nonpublic data to set or recommend rents, lease terms or occupancy. It is also unlawful for anyone to perform a coordinating function or to engage in or facilitate parallel pricing coordination. Municipalities may not enact conflicting ordinances.
rules.key_value: ban on algorithmic coordination of rents using competitors' nonpublic data
rules.quoted_span: a rental property owner, or any agent, representative, or subcontractor thereof, to receive, subscribe to, contract for, or otherwise exchange any form of consideration in return for the use of, the services of a coordinator;
rules.effective_date_note: Act takes effect on the first day of the twelfth month next following enactment; approved July 20, 2026, so July 1, 2027.
rules.exemptions: Excludes research/statistical use not used to set rents, free public rent estimates, equal-terms brokerage listing databases, government affordability controls; spreadsheets without AI requiring human analysis and plain database queries are not algorithmic devices; inpatient medical, long-term care and detention facilities are not residential dwelling units.
rules.penalty: Violation of the New Jersey Antitrust Act; remedies under P.L.1970, c.73 sections 6-17 (C.56:9-6 to 9-17) remain applicable; Attorney General complaint portal.
rules.interaction: Section 6(b) prohibits municipalities from enacting ordinances that conflicting with the act, which may affect Jersey City and Hoboken algorithmic ordinances.
rules.conflict_note: May preempt conflicting local ordinances (e.g., Jersey City, Hoboken) once effective; whether those ordinances conflict is uncertain.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to rental property owners and coordinators for residential dwelling units statewide.

unverifiable_exemptions: licensed long-term care, inpatient medical, detention facilities

parsed.doc_summary: NJ FAIR Act, P.L.2026, c.43 (approved 2026-07-20, effective 2027-07-01), bans algorithmic coordination of residential rent pricing as an Antitrust Act violation and bars conflicting municipal ordinances.
